sections.h2: Where is Middletown, NJ, and what shapes its housing?
sections.html:
Middletown is a township in northern Monmouth County and the county's largest municipality by population. Wikipedia gives it 58.72 square miles in total, of which 40.95 are land and 17.78 are water, mostly Sandy Hook Bay, Raritan Bay and the Navesink River. That water frontage explains why a good share of its houses sit near the shoreline or on creek lots.

The township was formed on October 31, 1693 and incorporated under the Township Act of 1798. Railroad service arrived in 1875, and the area slowly turned from fishing and farming villages into a commuter suburb. The township website lists five historic districts: Chapel Hill, Locust, Monmouth Hills, Navesink and Middletown Village.

The township spans eleven ZIP codes, and their postal names include Middletown, Belford, Lincroft, Locust, Navesink, Port Monmouth and Leonardo. A mailing address with one of those names can still sit inside the Township of Middletown for tax purposes, so check the block and lot rather than the postal town.

sections.h2: Which Middletown office does what with property tax?
sections.html:
Middletown splits the job between an assessment office and a collection division, and both sit in the Finance Department at 1 Kings Highway, Middletown, NJ 07748. Assessment questions go to the Tax Assessor, and the collector bills and collects only.

  • Tax Collection: 732-615-2086. Payment hours run 8:00 AM to 3:45 PM and office hours are 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, Monday to Friday, per the township collection page.
  • Tax Assessor: handles value, ownership and address changes, and senior and veteran relief paperwork. The township's assessment page links to the Monmouth County record search for assessed values, sales and property record cards.
  • Sewerage Authority: 732-495-1010 for delinquent sewer charges, which are billed separately from the tax bill.

The township says the bill combines municipal, library, school, open space and county taxes. Because those levies come from different bodies, the Middletown collector cannot explain a school or county budget line and will direct you to the taxing authority.

sections.h2: What are the Middletown property tax due dates and the grace period?
sections.html:
Middletown taxes are due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1. A 10-day grace period normally applies, and a tenth day that lands on a weekend or holiday pushes the deadline to the following business day. The last moment to pay without interest is 3:45 PM on the final day of the grace period.

The township states that the State of New Jersey does not accept postmarks, so a payment must be in the office on time. Interest on late payments is governed by N.J.S.A. 54:4-66. Failing to receive a bill does not cancel the tax under N.J.S.A. 54:4-64, so the owner is responsible for asking the collector what is due.

Bills go out once a year. The first-half amount is a preliminary half of the previous year's taxes, and the second-half bill subtracts that estimate from the final total once the rate is set. The collection page asks sellers to hand the bill to the new owner or the buyer's paying agent at closing. A duplicate bill carries a charge.

sections.h2: How does the Middletown tax sale work, and how does it affect a seller?
sections.html:
Every New Jersey municipality must hold at least one tax sale a year, and Middletown runs an accelerated electronic sale. For 2026 the township listed December 17, 2026 as the sale date. Payments received after 3:45 PM on November 10, 2026 had to be guaranteed funds such as an attorney trust check, title company check, cashier's check or money order, and card or ACH payments were unavailable after that time.

An unpaid parcel picks up added costs once it enters the sale process:

  • A 2% cost of sale, with a $15 minimum and a $100 maximum.
  • A $25 mailing fee for each of two scheduled mailings.
  • Delinquent taxes plus interest, added to those fees for the total due.

The township says these fees cannot be waived, and a notice that goes astray does not void the sale. It also warns that a tax lien gives the buyer no right to possess the property, which comes only through foreclosure. A seller who is behind should ask the collector for an exact payoff and give it to the title company early. Cash payments must be exact, because excess cash goes to the next quarter and no change is returned.

sections.h2: How did Middletown's 2026 assessments change, and how are appeals filed?
sections.html:
The township reports that the aggregate preliminary net value of Middletown for tax year 2026 was 7.94% above 2025. Higher total value does not mean every bill rises by that percentage, because the rate falls as total value climbs. An owner whose assessment grew less than 7.94% takes on a smaller share of the municipal levy, and one whose assessment grew more takes on a larger share.

The same page gives the appeal window for 2026 assessments: January 15, or April 1 if the assessment exceeds $1 million. Monmouth County uses an alternate calendar, so the statewide April 1 date does not govern ordinary houses here. Petitions can be filed through secure.njappealonline.com. Changes agreed with the assessor after May 15, 2026 take effect in tax year 2027.

Before filing, compare your value with closed sales on the township's interactive sales map, which leaves out distressed sales. The state's appeal guide says property taxes cannot be appealed, only the assessment, and that evidence should be dated before the October 1 assessment date.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show for Middletown homeowners?
sections.html:
Middletown is a heavily owner-occupied suburb with high incomes and long commutes, according to Census QuickFacts.

Middletown township figures from the Census Bureau, 2020-2024 survey period

Households25,211

With about 86% of occupied homes lived in by their owners, most Middletown sales involve a family selling a primary residence, and many include a mortgage payoff alongside any tax balance.

sections.h2: Does Middletown's historic designation affect a sale?
sections.html:
It can. The township's Landmarks Commission reviews work on structures inside the five historic districts, and owners planning additions or changes need a Certificate of Appropriateness. A buyer of a house in Middletown Village, Navesink, Locust, Chapel Hill or Monmouth Hills should know that exterior plans may go through that review.

Houses outside those districts follow ordinary township permit rules. If you are unsure which applies, ask the township with the block and lot number from your tax bill.

faqs.q: When is the last day to pay Middletown property tax without interest?
faqs.a: It is the last day of a 10-day grace period after each due date of February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, by 3:45 PM. A weekend or holiday on the tenth pushes the deadline to the following business day.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Middletown house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask the Middletown tax collector for a payoff figure, and your closing agent settles it out of the sale money. If the parcel has entered the tax sale process, added costs apply and guaranteed funds are required.

faqs.q: What is the appeal deadline for a Middletown assessment?
faqs.a: For 2026 assessments the township lists January 15, or April 1 when the assessment is over $1 million. Monmouth County follows an alternate calendar, and filing can be done through secure.njappealonline.com.

faqs.q: Who do I contact if my Middletown sewer bill is overdue?
faqs.a: Call the Township of Middletown Sewerage Authority at 732-495-1010. Delinquent sewer charges are separate from the property tax bill, and the township said it would sell delinquent sewer charges in 2026.

faqs.q: Does a postmark count for a Middletown tax payment?
faqs.a: No. The township says New Jersey does not accept postmarks, so the payment must be received in the office by 3:45 PM on or before the last day of the grace period.
